description: A string s is happy if it does not contain "aaa", "bbb", or "ccc" as a substring. Given three integers a, b, and c representing the maximum number of a, b, and c characters, return the longest possible happy string. If multiple answers exist, return any.
intuition: Always pick the character with the most remaining uses, unless it would create three in a row. In that case, insert one of the second-most frequent character as a separator. A max-heap efficiently tracks which character to use next.
approach: Use a greedy approach with a max-heap. Always try to use the character with the highest remaining count, unless it would create three consecutive same characters. In that case, use the second most frequent character.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: a=1, b=1, c=7

Initial heap: [[7,"c"],[1,"a"],[1,"b"]] (max-heap by count)

Iter 1: pop [7,"c"], result=[], no lastTwo -> append "c", push [6,"c"]
  result=["c"]

Iter 2: pop [6,"c"], result has only 1 item -> append "c", push [5,"c"]
  result=["c","c"]

Iter 3: pop [5,"c"], lastTwo=true (cc) -> pop [1,"a"], append "a", push [5,"c"] back
  result=["c","c","a"]

Iter 4: pop [5,"c"], no lastTwo (ca) -> append "c", push [4,"c"]
  result=["c","c","a","c"]

Iter 5: pop [4,"c"], no lastTwo (ac) -> append "c", push [3,"c"]
  result=["c","c","a","c","c"]

Iter 6: pop [3,"c"], lastTwo=true (cc) -> pop [1,"b"], append "b", push [3,"c"]
  result=["c","c","a","c","c","b"]

Iter 7: pop [3,"c"], no lastTwo (cb) -> append "c", push [2,"c"]
  result=["c","c","a","c","c","b","c"]

Iter 8: pop [2,"c"], no lastTwo (bc) -> append "c", push [1,"c"]
  result=["c","c","a","c","c","b","c","c"]

Return "ccaccbcc"
explanation:
1. Use a max-heap (negate counts for Python's min-heap).
2. Pop the character with the highest remaining count.
3. If appending it would create three in a row, use the second most frequent instead.
4. Push characters back with updated counts if they still have remaining uses.
5. Stop when no valid character can be appended.
hints: Greedily use the most frequent character to maximize length.
If the most frequent would create three in a row, use the second most frequent.
A max-heap efficiently tracks the most frequent character.
